lastPrompt: This project is an undergraduate compiler for the SysY language (a C subset) that translates source code into Koopa IR and RISC-V assembly. The compiler is written in Rust and uses the `lalrpop` parser generator along with the `koopa` IR library. It supports expressions (arithmetic, logical with short-circuit evaluation), control flow (if/else, while, break, continue), functions (definitions, calls, parameters), variable/constant declarations, and arrays (including multi-dimensional). Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present. The compiler binary is built with `cargo build --release` and called as: `/workspace/target/release/compiler-lab -koopa <input.c> -o <output.koopa>` `/workspace/target/release/compiler-lab -riscv <input.c> -o <output.asm>` The compiler has two main subsystems that need to be implemented: the IR builder (frontend) and the assembly builder (backend). Functions marked with `todo!()` need complete implementations. Implement the following modules: IR Builder — Compilation Unit (`src/ir_builder/mod.rs`): The top-level IR generation entry point. Responsible for declaring SysY library functions (getint, getch, getarray, putint, putch, putarray, starttime, stoptime) and building all compilation units. (~1 function to implement) IR Builder — Declarations (`src/ir_builder/build_declarations.rs`): Translates function definitions, variable declarations (local and global), and constant declarations into Koopa IR. Handles parameter allocation, symbol table management, array type construction, aggregate initializer flattening, and storing aggregate values element-by-element into local allocations. (~4 functions to implement) IR Builder — Expressions (`src/ir_builder/build_expressions.rs`): Translates SysY expressions into Koopa IR values. Covers binary operations with constant folding, logical OR/AND with short-circuit evaluation using basic blocks, unary expressions (plus, minus, not), function calls with parameter type checking, primary expressions (lvalues, numbers, parenthesized), and multi-dimensional array element access via getelemptr/getptr. (~5 functions to implement) IR Builder — Statements (`src/ir_builder/build_statements.rs`): Translates all SysY statement types into Koopa IR: assignments, expression statements, blocks, if/else with branch/jump wiring, while loops with break/continue target block stacks, break, continue, and return statements. (~1 large function to implement) Assembly Builder — Code Generation (`src/assembly_builder/build_assembly.rs`): The backend that converts Koopa IR programs into RISC-V assembly. Generates `.data`/`.text` sections for global variables and functions. Translates each IR instruction kind (return, binary, alloc, store, load, jump, branch, call, getptr, getelemptr) into the corresponding RISC-V instructions. Maps IR binary operations to RISC-V opcodes. Handles global aggregate initialization. (~4 functions to implement) Assembly Builder — Register Management (`src/assembly_builder/mod.rs`): Implements the register allocator and value table that manages how IR values are mapped to RISC-V registers using an LRU eviction strategy. Provides stack frame offset calculations for store/load/add operations (handling both short and long immediate offsets), register spilling to memory, LRU-based temporary register allocation, value-to-register loading (integers, globals, locals), value assignment between registers, absolute address computation for array elements, and saving/restoring global and local variables at basic block boundaries. (~9 functions to implement) After implementing all functions, rebuild with `cargo build --release` before running tests. You are running as a long-horizon autonomous engineering agent at `/workspace`. This task spans many files and requirements, and is expected to take many iterations.
